description: Erection of front boundary wall with railings and gate to a maximum height of 3m.
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:2024/1662/1MWA Tree Survey Schedule 2024/1662/32024/1662/22024/1662/3PLANNING STATEMENT Arboricultural Appraisal Report Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Unless otherwise specified in the application the materials to be used for the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted along with work of making good shall be carried out in materials to match those of the existing building.   Reason: To ensure that the appearance of the development respects the appearance, existing materials and built and natural features of the surrounding area.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including all preparatory work), a scheme for the protection of all retained trees compliant with BS 5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme will comprise a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) report supplemented by Tree Protection Plan(s) (TPP). The plan(s) shall be of legible scale and clearly show the layout (as agreed), all relevant existing site features that form a consideration within the protection scheme, and the location/extent of all appropriate protection measures.a) location and installation methodology of all utility services/drainage, avoiding the Root Protection Areas (RPA) of all retained trees as far as possible (RPA as defined within BS 5837:2012). The installation methodology shall demonstrate adherence to Street Works UK Publications Volume 4 (Guidelines for the planning, installation, and maintenance of Utility apparatus in proximity to Trees replaces NJUG Vol.4);b) methods of removal of existing hard standing within or directly adjacent to RPAs;c) a full specification for the construction of hard surfacing (including alterations to the existing layout of internal hard standing) within RPAs. Where a no-dig sub-base is specified (e.g. cellular confinement system) a specification shall be provided (including a diagrammatical cross-section of the product in-situ) and extent of areas where this would be implemented illustrated within the TPP;d) detailed levels and cross-sections to show the raised levels of surfacing where the installation of no-dig surfacing within RPAs is proposed, demonstrating that the raised areas can be effectively integrated with the operation of the gates, and prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing i.e. remainder of driveway, crossover installation;e) a full and detailed specification for the design and installation of the pier bases within or directly adjacent to RPAs, to include but not be limited to cross section diagrams, extent of excavation, methodology for preliminary testing for roots in proposed pier locations and where they will be moved to if roots are encountered;f) a full and detailed specification for the design and installation of the no dig railing bases within or directly adjacent to RPAs. All railings within the RPA shall be installed in this manner, and not only the set closest to the tree;g) a specification for protective fencing and, if necessary, ground protection, to safeguard all trees during both demolition and construction phases. The Tree Protection Plan(s) shall clearly indicate the alignment of the fencing and extent of ground protection;h) details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of equipment, materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and siting of fires; The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details.The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details.Reason: To satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality, in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

a) Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including all preparatory work), an auditable schedule of arboricultural supervision and inspection of tree protection measures by a suitably qualified arboriculturist shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This will include supervision of the installation of pier bases and railing bases, and the no dig surfacing, within the RPA of T1 Oak Tree as identified in the Arboricultural Appraisal Report. b) Upon the completion of each supervision visit and prior to the first use of the development hereby approved, a summary report prepared by a qualified arboriculturist shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Each report shall set out the findings of the supervision visit and any agreed actions and timescales arising therefrom, supplemented by photographs where appropriate. This condition shall not be discharged until it has been demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority that all works have been carried out in full compliance with the approved Arboricultural Method StatementReason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and ensure compliance with the agreed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS), to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
